title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: many cognitive experiments, want know whether stimulus pattern influences behavior even participants aware . test , researchers often collect two paired measures participants: direct task (asking directly whether noticed masked stimulus statistical regularity) indirect task (measuring behavioral effect, priming faster response times). uSDT package brings paired data together hierarchical Signal Detection Theory (SDT) framework, helping test key hypotheses unconscious processing within single unified model. tutorial, walk three straightforward steps: Prepare data: Use usdt_data_tasks() usdt_data_long() get paired measures ready modeling. Fit model: Run hsdt() fit hierarchical SDT model. model estimates overall task sensitivities, subject-specific sensitivity values, tests three key hypotheses unconscious processing. Inspect results: Visualize key model estimates plot(), quantify reliability group subject-specific levels usdt_reliability(), add parametric bootstrap inference usdt_boot() needed.

title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: usdt_data_tasks() combines two tasks single paired dataset. specify subject, condition, response columns, map levels signal noise roles. Whenever argument shared across tasks, can pass single value (like subject_col = "subj"). tasks differ, provide list per task using list(direct = ..., indirect = ...):
code: data_usdt <- usdt_data_tasks(   # One data frame per task   direct   = vadillo_awareness,   indirect = vadillo_cuing,    # Shared subject column   subject_col = "subj",    # Condition mapping (shared column name and labels here)   condition_col    = "condition",   condition_levels = c(signal = "old", noise = "new"),    # Response columns differ: judgements vs continuous response times   response_col = list(direct = "judged.old", indirect = "rt"),    # How responses map to signal vs noise   response_levels = list(     direct   = c(signal = 1, noise = 0),     indirect = c(signal = "faster", noise = "slower")   ),    # Dichotomize continuous response times using a median split   dichotomize = list(direct = FALSE, indirect = TRUE),      # Contrast coding scheme across conditions (deviation by-default)   coding = "deviation" )

title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: coding argument affects response criterion (also called “bias parameter”) represents model. Task sensitivity (d′d') remains identical schemes: "deviation" (default): Codes signal +0.5+0.5 noise −0.5-0.5. intercept reflects overall response bias centered stimulus distributions. "treatment": Codes noise 00 signal 11. intercept reflects criterion relative baseline (noise) condition. default, uSDT uses deviation coding.

title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: Setting dichotomize = list(direct = FALSE, indirect = TRUE) converts continuous RTs binary responses via median split computed within subject across trials, following approach proposed Meyen et al. (2022). case: RTs subject’s median count "faster" (signal responses). "hit" old display searched faster median, "false alarm" new display searched faster median. design, splitting exactly median balances fast slow responses across trials. deviation coding, balance centers indirect decision criterion zero (c≈0c \approx 0). , hsdt() fixes indirect criterion zero default whenever mean absolute subject criterion 0.02 (can override fix_criteria = "none").
